method: A heat flux density is a power divided by an area, so every unit reduces to the SI unit watt per square metre by one exact factor and nothing here depends on a measurement. The watt per square metre is the base; the kilowatt is 1000 and the milliwatt 0.001; a square centimetre is 1e-4 m² and a square inch 0.00064516 m², so W/cm² is 10 000 W/m², mW/cm² is 10 W/m² and W/in² is 1550.0031 W/m². The Btu is the International Table Btu of exactly 1055.05585262 J, the calorie the thermochemical calorie of exactly 4.184 J, the hour 3600 s and the foot 0.3048 m, which gives Btu/(h·ft²) = 1055.05585262 / (3600 × 0.09290304) = 3.154590745 W/m², Btu/(s·ft²) = 11 356.52668 W/m², cal/(s·cm²) = 41 840 W/m² and kcal/(h·m²) = 1.1622222 W/m². Results keep six significant digits, trailing zeros are trimmed and thousands are grouped; a magnitude below 1e-6 or from 1e12 up is written in exponential form. Zero is accepted because a surface can carry no heat flow; negative values are refused because a heat flux density has a direction, and anything above 1e9 W/m² is outside the supported range. Typed input may carry grouping commas but not a unit. All arithmetic runs in the browser and the page makes no network request.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 811 (2008 edition), Guide for the Use of the International System of Units (SI), Appendix B.9 factors for units listed by kind of quantity — Density of Heat Flow Rate: BtuIT/(ft²·h) = 3.154 591 W/m², BtuIT/(ft²·s) = 1.135 653 E+04 W/m², calth/(cm²·s) = 4.184 E+04 W/m², W/in² = 1.550 003 E+03 W/m² and W/cm² = 1.0 E+04 W/m²
Wikipedia, Heat flux: heat flux density is the rate of energy flow per unit area, with the SI unit W/m² and Btu/(h·ft²) as another unit
